doc.title: Jimmy Lewis interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

title: Hair closes, stolen bass book, royalties and Three Sparks and a Flame
summary: Butler closes the show; Lewis's bass book is stolen and he is owed money; he forms Three Sparks and a Flame and plans a Broadway musical.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: well so I came to see what was happening.” So they said, “we don’t know nothing about that.” They said, “it’s been packed every day and night.” He said, “okay,” so he went up in the big office and talked to some of the people, and told them, “the show is closed as of this minute.” So he closed the show out. Man, but four days before he closed it, somebody stole my bass book. All the other books were there, but my bass book was gone. And so I went down to one of the record companies we were doing business with, and I happened to see all these books on the floor piled up, you know all these books. Music, Galt’s music. So I said look at this. So I peeked in and I looked at it, and I seen my bass lines there, among all the music you know. So I went back and told Gordon. Gordon didn’t know anything about it either you know. But I tried to get some money back. So then that’s when we had a little lawyer, he shaked them and found out how much they’ve sat on. And he told me he said, “you know how much money you’ve got coming?” I said, “no.” He said, “you should have about a quarter of a million dollars.” I said, “what!” He said, “it’s over eight million in records, two years ago.” I said, “oh man.” So well you know that’s part of business. And so I tried and I couldn’t get anything to happen with that. So then “Hair” closed. It closed and I decided I’d form me up a little group, a jazz group called Three Sparks and a Flame. Well she was the flame, and so over there, I had wrote about, oh over a hundred tunes at that time. I’ve got more now. But we decided we were going to do all our tunes. But we ended up doing a lot of Basie and Duke and all these different arrangements you know. I would arrange all the stuff, and set it to the style I wanted. And we could make a trio sound like an eight piece band. No horns. We could do that. And so we got pretty popular. We started getting all these big jobs you know around town. And they called us, in a place called Cafe Society. It was down on 22nd Street and Broadway I think. And we went down there and stayed there a while, and left there and went to another place on 54th Street. So we went in there for a while. And people liked it, they kept calling us back. So I took the group and so we decided we’d do our own booking. So I learned the business end of it. And we were getting a lot of good gigs you know, all these places way out in the suburbs, some places on Long Island, way out on Long Island. And the big golf clubs and all that. And so we did that for a long time, then I decided to do a video. I did a video but it didn’t turn out like I wanted. Now I’m working on a Broadway musical. But it’s going to be a different kind of musical from all these other musicals you’ve seen. It’s going to be like a play, it’s a love story. It’s going to be a play, and I wrote all the music for it, and I’m just kind of putting it together now.
Well you have had a marvelous, amazing career, and it’s still going, which we’re so glad to hear.
Yeah it seems like I’m going to be all right.
